newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar polls could lead to more democracy - emir.
newsitem.headline: Qatar polls could lead to more democracy - emir.

text.p: Qatar's plans to hold municipal elections might open the way for a wider democractic process in the Gulf Arab state, Qatar's Emir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa al-Thani said.
"We are going to have municipal elections and we would like to see how it goes," he said in an interview with Cable News Network (CNN) aired on Sunday.
"We have a free press which is very important to see what the people think and want, but for the election process it would take a few years for us to go further."

He said the issue of whether women would be allowed to vote was still being discussed, but he supported the participation of women. "I hope women will vote. There is nothing wrong if they were allowed to vote," he said.
Qatar, whose native population of around 160,000 is outnumbered by nearly half a million expatriate workers, is the first Gulf Arab state to order municipal elections.
Officials said the polls would be held by November.
Asked whether he discussed the democratic process with other leaders in the Gulf, Sheikh Hamad said: "We discuss it sometimes, but it did not have any reaction."
Kuwait has the only elected parliament on the Arab side of the Gulf, but only men can vote. The emir of neighbouring Bahrain dissolved the island's elected legislature in 1975.
Qatar's municipal election was announced by Sheikh Hamad as a first step towards enlisting public support and developing democracy in his country.
Sheikh Hamad ousted his father, Sheikh Khalifa bin Hamad al-Thani, in a bloodless palace coup in June 1995. He refused to comment when asked in the interview about that.
